item.title: A pathway to improve Nb$_3$Sn for SRF accelerator cavities via Zr inclusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.36479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nb$_3$Sn has the potential to exceed the performance of niobium-based superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) cavities, both in particle accelerators and in high-$Q_0$ cavities operating in multi-tesla magnetic fields for axion dark matter searches. We studied how the incorporation of Zr into the Nb$_3$Sn matrix by co-sputtering affects the microstructure and superconducting properties of Nb$_3$Sn films. As the atomic fraction of Zr increased, the surface morphology improved and the bulk and surface void densities decreased. At the optimal Zr content, the superconducting properties improved and a thinner surface niobium oxide formed. These results identify co-sputtered Nb$_3$Sn:Zr as a promising material to advance the performance limits of SRF cavities.
item.dc:creator: M. Tripathi, M. S. Shakel, J. Lee, H. E. Elsayed-Ali, S. Posen, G. V. Eremeev

item.title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
item.description: arXiv:2610.37352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical Coulomb crystals and quantum Wigner crystals typically arise when repulsive interactions order like-charged particles in spatially confined environments. Here, we show that transient crystallization can also emerge in freely propagating electron pulses without external trapping. Experimentally, we use a transmission electron microscope to measure number-resolved energy correlations in photoemitted pulses containing up to nine electrons, revealing strong correlations at small particle numbers that progressively disappear in the pulse interior as the number increases. To explain these observations, we combine many-body simulations with a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model, showing that the leading and trailing electrons generate a self-induced longitudinal potential that transiently confines the inner particles, enabling the formation of an ordered chain during propagation. The resulting crystallization phase diagram reveals how many-body ordering dynamics can be understood in terms of evolving macroscopic beam properties, namely its geometry and the ratio of the mean Coulomb interaction energy to the longitudinal thermal energy. Extending this framework, we theoretically demonstrate that weak transverse guiding through electrostatic or optical ponderomotive forces can sustain crystallization at larger particle numbers and predict spontaneous longitudinal periodic bunching in continuous electron beams. Our results identify conditions under which stochastic Coulomb interactions can be harnessed to generate self-structured, strongly correlated electron beams in both pulsed and continuous regimes.
item.dc:creator: Valerio Di Giulio, Rudolf Haindl, Armin Feist, Claus Ropers

item.title: Generalization of the Froissart-Stora formula to piecewise-linear spin-orbit resonance crossings
item.description: arXiv:2603.24510v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin-polarized beams are important for some nuclear and high-energy physics experiments, such as those planned for the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). However, maintaining polarization during the acceleration of a charged-particle beam is difficult because the periodic nature of circular accelerators leads to spin-orbit resonances where the spin-precession frequency is a sum of integer multiples of the orbital frequencies. Usually, the dominant depolarization mechanisms are first-order spin-orbit resonances and the depolarization associated with crossing such a resonance can be computed using the Froissart-Stora formula. However, accelerating polarized hadron beams to high energy requires special magnet structures called Siberian snakes. When these are implemented to maintain a spin-precession frequency of one-half the revolution frequency, there will be no first-order spin-orbit resonance crossings. The dominant depolarization mechanisms are then higher-order spin-orbit resonances. The Froissart-Stora formula can be applied to higher-order resonances when the slope of the amplitude-dependent spin tune is constant. However, the slope of the amplitude-dependent spin tune often changes at the moment of resonance crossing. This work introduces a generalization of the Froissart-Stora formula which is applicable when the slope changes in this manner. The applicability of this formula is demonstrated through tracking simulations of a higher-order resonance crossing in both a toy model and the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). It is additionally shown that the Froissart-Stora formula is mathematically equivalent to the Landau-Zener formula for the diabatic transition probability in two-level systems with a linearly increasing energy gap and constant coupling. This work therefore also extends the Landau-Zener formula to the case of changing slope.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. P. Devlin, G. H. Hoffstaetter, and D. P. Barber, "Generalization of the Froissart-Stora formula to piecewise-linear spin-orbit resonance crossings", Phys. Rev. Accel. Beams 29, 074702 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Joseph P. Devlin, Georg H. Hoffstaetter, Desmond P. Barber

item.title: Polarization-dependent exchange effects in intrabeam scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.24245v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The emittance growth due to intrabeam scattering (IBS) depends on the scattering cross section and is therefore affected by the exchange interaction of identical particles. However, as the IBS growth rates are typically dominated by small-angle scattering events and the exchange interaction only significantly alters the cross section at relatively large angles, the influence of the exchange interaction is usually small. In this paper, we calculate the small corrections to the growth rates resulting from the exchange interaction. We include the polarization dependence of the exchange term in the cross section, and so we also present the growth rates as a function of the beam polarization.
item.dc:creator: Joseph P. Devlin, Georg H. Hoffstaetter
